rules: Import `ruststream_kinesis::prelude::*` in the file that mounts handlers; a handler body keeps `ruststream::prelude::*` and learns no broker, except the one body that names a per-message setting.
Name the stream with `KinesisStream::new("orders")` inside `#[subscriber(..)]`; the bare `#[subscriber("orders")]` form builds the same descriptor with its default read settings.
Price a read on the descriptor or at the mount site with the same two methods, `poll_interval(d)` and `create_if_missing(shards)`; they chain before `start_at(..)`, which replaces the descriptor.

A record's partition key is a per-message setting: `.partition_key(..)` on the publish builder for a call that has one, and on the policy at the mount site (`.out_reply(Publish::default()).partition_key(..)`) for a reply, which has none.
The one handler body that names a broker is the one that sets the key: it imports this crate's prelude and bounds its slot as `Out<impl Publisher<Options = KinesisPublishOptions>, Marker>`.

Nothing about redelivery is native here, so `.max_attempts(n)` and `.dead_letter(name)` make the framework publish a copy back to the stream; the copy arrives at the tip, so an order-sensitive handler returns `HandlerOutcome::retry()` and lets the shard replay instead.

`ack` is a per-shard checkpoint covering every earlier record and delivery is at-least-once; it is written to the lease store, `MemoryLeaseStore` in process by default and `DynamoLeaseStore` behind the `dynamodb-lease` feature when several service instances share the shards.

A lease and a checkpoint belong to a stream and a shard together (`LeaseKey`), so one lease store serves every stream a broker consumes; a `DynamoDB` lease table written by a version that keyed rows by the shard id alone is read through `DynamoLeaseStore::legacy_stream(stream)`, naming the one stream those rows belong to.

Open or move a subscription with `KinesisPosition` only: `start_at(..)` at the mount site and `Ctx<SeekHandle>` in a handler; a stream-wide position moves every shard, and a `sequence` one moves only the shard it names.

Test the production app: with feature `testing`, hand the builder `main` runs to `ruststream::testing::TestApp::start`, which connects `KinesisBroker` in process, and address it as `tb.broker::<KinesisBroker>()`; `TestApp::start_live` runs the same test against a real stream, which is where shards, leases, checkpoints and resharding are exercised.

Kinesis offers no request/reply and no transactions, and enhanced fan-out and KPL deaggregation are not implemented; a stream's five reads a second per shard is the budget `poll_interval` and the batch size spend.
